newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares soar on rate cut, peso strength.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares soar on rate cut, peso strength.

text.p: Manila shares were sharply higher on Friday, bolstered by another interest rate cut, and analysts said the market may reap further gains next week if the peso continues to gain strength.

"I'm pleased to tell you that the Philippines is alive and the principal reason is that the peso-dollar rate has stabilised a little bit, though not fully. Overnight rates have been lowered again," said Irving Ackerman, president at I. Ackerman & Co Inc.
The main index closed firmer for the second day on Friday, up 52.57 points, or 2.01 percent, at 2,672.95 points.

Philippine shares were reeling for the first few days of the week as equities investors, driven out by high interest rates and lingering concerns on the direction of the peso-dollar exchange rate, sought refuge in higher yield fixed-income instruments.
The Central Bank late on Thursday lowered overnight borrowing rates by three percentage points to 25 percent, the second cut since the de facto devaluation of the peso last Friday.
On Friday morning, the peso had recovered to 27.80 after falling to 30 early in the week.

"The pressure is off on the equities market with this cut in overnight rates. People are moving back and repositioning, and there's a lot more buying on the foreign side," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
Turnover was higher at 2.3 billion pesos on Friday from the previous day's 2.14 billion.

"Nerves are being calmed since the peso is now settling at a level that is not as bad as people thought. There will be a tendency next week for the market to make up for its losses," said one fund manager.

"So long as the Central Bank keeps on bringing down rates and the peso continues to consolidate at better levels, then there will be more buying," said Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Ruiz said the market will likely test a psychological resistance of 2,700 points next week.
Some traders said it may, however, be too drastic to say that the stock market will be in for a reversal.
"Despite the improvement in the market, there is still that air of caution. We've only had a few days of stability," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
Sun Hung Kai's Ruiz said investors would continue to discriminate in buying stocks, taking into account second quarter corporate earnings.
"Perhaps all we can say now is that the worst is over," Ackerman said.
